image_description: A man wearing a cowboy hat and blue shirt is holding a hammerhead shark on a boat. The shark's head (cephalofoil) is visible on the left, showing the characteristic hammer shape with eyes at the tips. The man is gripping the shark near its gills/head area. The background shows parts of a boat structure and sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hammer-shaped head is clearly visible on the left side of the image, extending laterally.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark eye spots are visible at the outer edges of the hammer-shaped head structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution and angle do not allow clear visualization of nostrils on the ventral/lateral surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the cephalofoil appears straight/slightly curved, consistent with hammerhead morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the shark's body behind the head shows a streamlined, compressed profile typical of sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is greyish-brown, and the underside/ventral area appears lighter/white where visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve individual dermal denticles; skin appears smooth due to compression/wetness.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is obscured by the man's body and the angle of the shot; only the head and anterior body are clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are not clearly visible in this framing; the focus is on the head and the man holding it.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail/caudal fin is completely out of frame or obscured.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The fingers merging into the shark's head/gill area lack clear definition. The thumb and fingers appear fused with the shark's skin, lacking distinct boundaries and anatomical correctness. The grip looks physically implausible with digits melting into the subject.

The fabric texture appears overly smooth and plastic-like in areas, with unnatural shading gradients that don't fully correspond to the lighting direction. The logo/text on the chest is indistinct and blurry.
The vertical poles and railings in the background show slight warping and inconsistent perspective lines, particularly where they intersect with the sky and other structures.

The open mouth area lacks clear internal structure (teeth, gums). It appears as a dark, undefined void merging with the surrounding tissue, lacking the sharp anatomical details expected in a close-up of a shark's head.
